findings.claim: In a Slate piece excerpted on the Election Law Blog, Rick Hasen reported that Bloomberg gave $64.3 million in the 2024 cycle, all but $1 million to the Democratic side, the biggest donor on that side. Forbes records that he was mayor of New York from 2002 to 2013 and owns about 88% of Bloomberg LP.

The New York Times reported in October 2026 that Bloomberg had given about $80 million to Democratic candidates and groups in September and October 2026, including $24 million to Everytown and $16 million to House Majority PAC. The figures came from his team before the filings were due.

FEC data show about $1.09 billion of Bloomberg’s own money went into his 2020 campaign. Complaints said its $18 million transfer to the DNC evaded contribution limits; in May 2023 the FEC dismissed them as a matter of prosecutorial discretion, and commissioners saw no sign he meant to evade the limits.

In May 2020 the SEC found that Bloomberg Tradebook, then a broker unit, misled customers about an undisclosed order-routing arrangement used from 2010 to 2018. It was censured and paid a $5 million penalty, without admitting or denying the findings.

In January 2023 Bloomberg Finance paid a $5 million SEC penalty. The SEC said that from 2016 to 2022 it did not tell BVAL customers that some bond valuations could rest on a single input such as one broker quote; it settled without admitting or denying the findings.

The EEOC sued Bloomberg’s company in 2007, alleging a pattern of discrimination against pregnant employees. In August 2011 Judge Loretta Preska granted summary judgment against that pattern-or-practice claim, finding the evidence insufficient; individual claims could proceed, and Bloomberg was not named personally.

Former saleswoman Sekiko Sakai Garrison sued Bloomberg personally and his company in 1997 over alleged sexual harassment and discrimination, including a 1995 remark on her pregnancy he denied under oath; it was settled confidentially in 2000, without admission, over 25 years ago. In 2020 he released three women from NDAs over comments they said he made.

In May 2025 a Middlesex County jury found that Bloomberg’s 2020 campaign broke an oral promise of work through November 2020 to field organizer Nygel O’Bannon; the judgment, with interest and costs, was later set at about $53,750, and both sides appealed. In a related state case, Doty, a contract claim against the campaign is pending.

In June 2026 Judge Patti Saris (D. Mass.) let a former campaign worker pursue a claim that Bloomberg personally made an oral job promise on a call with staff; this is a pleading-stage ruling and he denies the promise under oath. In March 2026 a state judge had dismissed him personally from the related Doty case for lack of jurisdiction.

Authors led by Mike Huckabee allege that Bloomberg trained its BloombergGPT model on their copyrighted books without permission. In November 2025 a federal judge in New York denied Bloomberg’s motion to dismiss, saying fair use needs a factual record; the case is pending and nothing has been decided on the merits.
The Bloomberg Family Foundation reported charitable disbursements of about $1.47 billion in fiscal 2024 and $1.42 billion in 2023, according to its Form 990-PF filings.

The Chronicle of Philanthropy ranked Bloomberg first among US donors for 2025, with $4.3 billion, and put his lifetime giving, personally and through Bloomberg Philanthropies, at $25.4 billion. It counts multiyear gifts when announced and left out some larger givers, so this is not a disbursed total.

politics.reason: Gave $64.3 million in the 2024 cycle, all but $1 million to the Democratic side, the biggest donor on that side, and about $80 million in autumn 2026 by his team’s account. Put about $1.09 billion into his 2020 presidential run; the FEC dismissed complaints over an $18 million transfer to the DNC. Mayor of New York from 2002 to 2013 and owner of about 88% of Bloomberg LP, a major news organisation.

social.reason: A Massachusetts jury found in 2025 that his 2020 campaign broke a promise of work to a field organizer; the verdict is on appeal. The SEC found that Bloomberg units misled customers on order routing (2020) and failed to disclose bond-valuation practices (2023), settled without admission. An EEOC pattern-of-pregnancy-bias claim against his company was dismissed in 2011. In 2020 he released three women from NDAs over comments they said he made.

legal.reason: Bloomberg was a named defendant in a harassment and discrimination suit filed in 1997 and settled confidentially in 2000, without admission; he denied the claims. At company level, Bloomberg units paid $5 million SEC penalties in 2020 and 2023 without admitting the findings, and the EEOC’s pattern-of-discrimination claim was dismissed in 2011. The FEC dismissed complaints about his campaign’s transfer to the DNC in 2023. No penalty against him personally was found.

unresolved.reason: Since June 2026 a federal court in Massachusetts has let a former campaign worker pursue a contract claim against Bloomberg personally, at the pleading stage; he denies making the promise. Related claims against his 2020 campaign, including an appealed jury verdict, are pending. A copyright suit over training BloombergGPT on authors’ books is pending against Bloomberg L.P. and Bloomberg Finance after dismissal was denied in 2025.

proposal.counterweights: The Bloomberg Family Foundation reported about $1.47 billion in charitable disbursements in 2024 (Form 990-PF). The Chronicle of Philanthropy ranked him first among US donors for 2025, with $4.3 billion, counting multiyear pledges when announced.
